result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian access with sidewalks and marked zebra crosswalks, but lacks modern safety features like curb ramps or pedestrian signals. The building on the corner creates a potential sightline obstruction, and the pavement markings show signs of wear.

hazards.name: Lack of ADA accessibility
hazards.description: No visible curb ramps at the crossing points, creating a significant barrier for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corners of the intersection.

hazards.name: Restricted sightlines
hazards.description: The building on the left corner is built right up to the sidewalk, potentially creating a blind spot for drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Faded pavement markings
hazards.description: The crosswalk markings are somewhat worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main and side streets.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint crosswalks with high-visibility 'continental' or 'ladder' patterns to improve driver awareness.

result.summary: This residential street features a wide roadway with faded crosswalk markings and no active traffic control for pedestrians. Significant visual obstructions are present due to parked vehicles and a large truck positioned near the intersection, which compromises sightlines for those attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars and a large truck near the intersection severely limit the visibility between pedestrians and approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings

hazards.description: Cracked and patched pavement in the roadway may cause tripping hazards or vehicle swerving.

result.summary: The image shows a residential urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like curb ramps is present, the intersection lacks visible traffic control signals or stop signs, and parked vehicles near the corners may obstruct sightlines.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners limit the visibility between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street beyond the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: There are no visible stop signs or traffic signals to regulate vehicle flow at this marked crosswalk, creating ambiguity in right-of-way.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection of Diamond St and 32nd St.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and make pedestrians more visible to drivers.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and prioritize pedestrian movement.
